text:
Dylan Larkin isn't playing for the Red Wings, and that is the story of their season. He asked for a trade, was stripped of the captaincy, and was suspended without pay after he stopped reporting at the end of October, choosing to sit until Detroit moves him. Interim general manager Shawn Horcoff called it "status quo" this week, with defenseman Simon Edvinsson also unsigned and not playing. Reports have Montreal and Minnesota circling, but no deal.

Without their former captain the Red Wings are 8-10-3 with 19 points, and the frustrating part is the process. Detroit has taken 50% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances). It has just scored 11 fewer goals than those chances usually produce, a gap that size usually narrows with time, and our playoff odds are down to 19%.

The goaltending is split. John Gibson is at .851 and 4.8 goals worse than expected over his last five starts. Daniil Tarasov has been better than his record, 4.5 goals saved above expected over his.

There is life in the young forwards. Alex DeBrincat with Emmitt Finnie and Michael Brandsegg-Nygard has outscored teams 8-1 and taken 63% of the chances, and Moritz Seider has become the voice of a team without a captain. What we'd watch: whether a Larkin trade finally lands, and what comes back, because that decides what this season is for.
